planting.note: Transplant or direct-seed into flooded paddy once soil is consistently warm; its short cycle supports two to three crops per year in a true tropical climate.

directions: OM5451 was bred at the Cuu Long Delta Rice Research Institute (part of the Vietnam Academy of Agricultural Sciences) from a cross of the aromatic Jasmine 85 and OM2490 lines, and it has become one of the most widely planted commercial rice varieties in the Mekong Delta. It is a short-duration, semi-dwarf type that reaches maturity in roughly 93 to 102 days, carries useful resistance to brown planthopper and rice blast, and produces good milling quality suited to the export jasmine-rice trade. Transplant seedlings from a flooded nursery bed into puddled paddy soil kept consistently wet through tillering, then drain the field ahead of harvest; its short cycle is what allows Mekong Delta farmers to take two or three crops from the same field each year. Grow in full sun in a warm, humid climate essentially identical to other tropical lowland rice.
sources: Cuu Long Delta Rice Research Institute (Vietnam Academy of Agricultural Sciences) variety records
Vietnam Journal of Science and Technology — Study on flowering in rice plant Oryza sativa cv. OM5451

planting.note: Direct-seed or transplant into flooded paddy once soil is reliably warm; like its sibling ST25, this short-duration type allows multiple crops per year.

directions: ST24 is an aromatic jasmine-type rice bred in Sóc Trăng province in Vietnam's Mekong Delta by engineer Hồ Quang Cua and colleagues, part of the same long-running ST breeding line that later produced ST25. It was crowned best in the world at the 2019 Rice Trader World Rice Conference in Manila, after placing third at the same event in Macau in 2017, the first time a Vietnamese rice had ever topped the competition. The grain cooks up long, clear white, and fragrant with a hint of pineapple aroma, and the plant yields over five tonnes per hectare while tolerating brackish lower-delta soils better than many older varieties. Grow it exactly like other modern Mekong Delta paddy rice: transplant into flooded, puddled soil, keep shallow standing water through the vegetative stage, and drain before harvest.
sources: Báo Chính Phủ — ST24 recognized as world's most delicious rice
VietnamPlus — Soc Trang's rice variety recognised as best in world

common_name: NSIC Rc222 Rice (Tubigan 18, Philippine Irrigated Lowland Rice)

planting.note: Transplant or direct wet-seed into flooded paddy soil once it is reliably warm; this early-maturing variety performs well in both irrigated and rainfed lowland fields, especially during the wet season.

directions: NSIC Rc222, popularly marketed in the Philippines as Tubigan 18, was released in 2009-2010 through the Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) and National Seed Industry Council registration process, building on breeding lines developed with the International Rice Research Institute. It is an early-maturing inbred, reaching harvest in about 106 days under direct wet-seeding or 114 days when transplanted, with national trial yields averaging around 6 tons per hectare and reaching up to 10 tons per hectare under good management. The grain has intermediate amylose content with good milling and head-rice recovery, and the variety performs consistently across both irrigated and rainfed lowland conditions, showing its strongest yield advantage during the wet season. Grow it as standard lowland paddy rice: puddled, flooded soil through the vegetative stage, full sun, and a drained field before harvest.
sources: Philippine Rice Research Institute (PhilRice) — All-Season Rice Varieties for Transplanting and Direct Wet-Seeding
Pinoy Rice Knowledge Bank

common_name: HL518 Sweet Potato (Nhật Đỏ, Vietnamese Japanese-Red Sweet Potato)

planting.note: Plant rooted slips or vine cuttings 2-4 weeks after last frost once soil is warm; this Vietnamese commercial variety is grown on ridges exactly like other sweet potatoes.

directions: HL518 was bred at the Hưng Lộc Agricultural Research Center (part of the Institute of Agricultural Science and Technology for Southern Vietnam, under the Vietnam Academy of Agricultural Sciences) from a Kokey 14 polycross of Japanese origin, and it was officially recognized as a national variety by Vietnam's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in 1997 under the trade name Nhật Đỏ. The tuber has red skin and distinctly deep orange-yellow flesh with better boiled-tuber flavor and more uniform, slender tuber shape than comparable Vietnamese varieties, reaching harvest in 95 to 110 days with fresh yields of roughly 17 to 32 tons per hectare and 27 to 30 percent dry matter. Plant rooted slips into well-drained, ridged, sandy-loam soil in full sun, keeping the vigorous purple-green vines from rooting at every node if continued single-crown tuber size is wanted. It has become one of Vietnam's two leading modern sweet potato varieties, grown widely for both domestic eating and export.
sources: Can Tho University Journal of Science
Vietnam Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development variety recognition records, 1997

common_name: HL491 Sweet Potato (Nhật Tím, Vietnamese Japanese-Purple Sweet Potato)

planting.note: Plant rooted slips or vine cuttings 2-4 weeks after last frost once soil is warm, in ridged beds exactly like other sweet potatoes.

directions: HL491 was bred at the Hưng Lộc Agricultural Research Center from a Murasa Kimasari polycross imported from Japan in 1994, and it was officially recognized as a national Vietnamese variety by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development in 1997 under the trade name Nhật Tím. The tuber has purple skin and deep purple flesh, cooks with good eating quality, and is notably high in anthocyanin antioxidants, maturing in 95 to 110 days with fresh yields of about 15 to 27 tons per hectare and 27 to 31 percent dry matter. Plant rooted slips into well-drained, ridged, sandy-loam soil in full sun; the purple-tinted green vines grow vigorously and root readily at the nodes, so lift any rooted nodes periodically if larger primary tubers are preferred. It became widely grown in Vinh Long and other Mekong Delta provinces from the early 2000s and remains one of Vietnam's leading purple sweet potato varieties for both domestic and export markets.
sources: Can Tho University Journal of Science
Vietnam Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development variety recognition records, 1997

common_name: LD1 Dragon Fruit (Long Định 1, Vietnamese Red-Fleshed Pitaya)

planting.note: Plant rooted stem cuttings in spring after frost danger passes, against a sturdy post or trellis; this climbing cactus needs reliable warmth and cannot tolerate hard freezes.

directions: LD1, short for Long Định 1, was bred by the Southern Horticultural Research Institute (SOFRI) in Tiền Giang province, Vietnam, and released in 2005 as a sexual hybrid between a Bình Thuận white-fleshed mother and a red-fleshed Colombian father plant. It was one of the first red-fleshed dragon fruit cultivars developed specifically for the Vietnamese industry and remains a popular commercial and premium-export choice, valued for its vivid magenta skin and rich red flesh with a sweeter profile than older white-fleshed Vietnamese selections. As an epiphytic climbing cactus it needs very well-drained, sandy to loamy soil, a sturdy trellis or post for support, and only occasional deep watering rather than frequent irrigation. Grow it in full sun in a frost-free climate, or in a large container that can be sheltered during any cold spell outside the true tropics.
sources: Southern Horticultural Research Institute (SOFRI), Vietnam — fruit breeding program documentation
Vietnam Academy of Agricultural Sciences journal — Fruit Breeding for the South of Vietnam

common_name: LD5 Dragon Fruit (Long Định 5, Vietnamese Pink-Violet-Fleshed Pitaya)

planting.note: Plant rooted stem cuttings in spring after frost danger passes, against a sturdy post or trellis; this self-fertile selection sets fruit reliably without hand pollination.

directions: LD5, short for Long Định 5, was bred by the Southern Horticultural Research Institute (SOFRI) and released in December 2010 as a hybrid between the red-fleshed LD1 as mother and a white-fleshed Chợ Gạo selection as father. It produces oblong fruit with large green scales, averaging 350 to 400 grams, filled with attractive pink-violet flesh carrying 16 to 18 degrees Brix sugar content, notably sweeter than most white-fleshed Vietnamese dragon fruit, along with good tolerance of several common diseases and reliably self-fertile flowers that set fruit without hand pollination. As an epiphytic climbing cactus it needs very well-drained, sandy to loamy soil, a sturdy trellis or post, and only occasional deep watering. Grow it in full sun in a frost-free climate, or in a large container that can be moved under cover during any cold spell.
sources: Southern Horticultural Research Institute (SOFRI), Vietnam — fruit breeding program documentation
Vietnam Academy of Agricultural Sciences journal — Fruit Breeding for the South of Vietnam

common_name: Guimaras Super Mango (Galila, Philippines' Sweetest Carabao Mango Strain)

planting.note: Plant a grafted tree in spring in full sun on well-drained soil; it shares the vigorous, upright growth habit of other Carabao-type mangos and needs a frost-free climate or large container with winter shelter.

directions: Guimaras Super, also called Galila after the grower who selected it on Guimaras Island, is the sweetest of roughly 15 registered Carabao mango strains documented at the Guimaras National Crop Research, Development and Production Support Center, testing around 22.3 degrees Brix compared to 18.98 for the next-sweetest named strain. The fruit is notably large for a Carabao-type mango, with meaty, smooth, firm, juicy, non-fibrous flesh, a slightly thicker peel than other strains, and a thin seed that leaves most of the fruit edible. Guimaras mangos as a group, including this strain, were approved as the Philippines' first registered Geographical Indication by the Intellectual Property Office in 2023, reflecting the island's distinct growing conditions. Grow and manage it exactly like other grafted Carabao mango trees: full sun, deep well-drained soil, a pronounced dry period before flowering, and frost protection or container culture outside the true tropics.
sources: Philippine Star — Guimaras Super Galila, the sweetest Carabao mango
Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines — IPOPHL OKs Guimaras Mangoes as PH's first GI

common_name: IPB Pag-asa 7 Mung Bean (UPLB-Bred Early-Maturing Philippine Mungbean)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost once soil reaches 65°F; this fast, early-maturing variety suits successive warm-season plantings.

directions: Pag-asa 7 is part of a long-running series of mungbean varieties bred by the Institute of Plant Breeding at the University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB-IPB), a program credited with raising mungbean yields and disease resistance not only in the Philippines but in Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Myanmar, and South Korea. It is an early-maturing selection, reaching harvest in just 62 to 74 days after emergence, with shiny green seeds, medium-sized black pods, moderate resistance to Cercospora leaf spot, and useful tolerance of drought stress. Direct sow seeds an inch deep in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun, and inoculate with Rhizobium for best nitrogen fixation. Harvest when pods dry and turn blackish-brown, and expect a compact, upright, bushy plant typical of modern mungbean breeding lines rather than a sprawling landrace habit.
sources: UPLB Institute of Plant Breeding variety documentation
Status of Mungbean Production in Central Luzon, Philippines

common_name: UPL Bs3 Bush Sitao (UPLB Trellis-Free Philippine Bush Yardlong Bean)

planting.note: Sow 2-6 weeks after last frost once soil is warm; unlike climbing yardlong bean, this compact bush type needs no trellis and tolerates wind better.

directions: UPL Bs3, known commercially as Bush Sitao, was bred at the Institute of Plant Breeding, University of the Philippines Los Baños (UPLB-IPB), as a semi-bush cross between climbing yardlong bean and bush-type cowpea, intended to replace trellised sitao as the preferred home-garden form in the Philippines. The compact, self-supporting plant produces light green, 6 to 8 inch pods in as few as 60 days, with a firm cooked texture and semi-sweet flavor similar to standard yardlong bean, but the bushy habit resists wind damage and eliminates the need for a trellis or fence. Direct sow seeds an inch deep in well-drained, warm soil in full sun, and pick pods young and pencil-thin for the best eating quality, checking plants every day or two once pods begin to set since they mature quickly. Its compact form makes it well suited to small home gardens and container culture where a full-size climbing yardlong bean would be impractical.
sources: UPLB Institute of Plant Breeding — Bush Sitao (UPL Bs3) variety listing
ECHOcommunity — Yardlong Bean technical note
